h1: The 7 Best Bookshelves with Drawers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bookshelves with Drawers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 bookshelves with drawers scored on drawer type, footprint and capacity, from slide-out cabinets to fabric-bin units.
summary: The FINETONES 71-inch Double Wide is the most storage you can get in one unit, with four real drawers and eight open shelves. For a taller, narrower build, the DICTAC adds three slide-out drawers on a 73-inch frame. On a tight budget, the Furologee 5-Tier with one removable fabric drawer fits almost any corner. Renting or parenting a toddler? Fabric drawers beat sliding rails.
intro: Most bookshelves hand you a pile of open shelves and call it storage. The trouble starts the day you own more small stuff than books: chargers, remotes, mail, craft supplies. Open shelves turn that into visible clutter, which is the whole reason a drawer exists.

We reviewed seven shelving units that pair open display space with closed storage, from rail-mounted drawers to lift-out fabric bins. Each was ranked on how much it actually stores, how wide it stands, how the drawer works and what the frame is made of, using the spec sheets and what owners report.

products.name: FINETONES 71" Double Wide Bookshelf + 4 Drawers
products.verdict: Four drawers plus eight open shelves in one wide, rigid frame. It swallows a whole room's clutter.
products.description:
The FINETONES is a double-wide unit, 39.4 inches across and about 71 inches tall, with four wrap-around drawers and eight open shelves. That adds up to twelve separate storage zones, and each shelf is rated for roughly 9 to 12 books at about 38 lb.

It tops this ranking because no other pick pairs real drawers with this much open shelf space. The DICTAC below is taller but narrower and holds fewer open books, and the fabric-bin models give up rigidity. The price of all that room is footprint: you need nearly 40 inches of clear wall and a bit more than a foot of depth.

Buy it for a living room, office or bedroom wall where one piece of furniture should replace a bookcase and a dresser. Skip it if your wall is narrow.
pros: Twelve storage zones in one unit
Four real drawers with metal handles
products.idealFor: People who want one wall unit to replace a bookcase and a dresser.
products.skipIf: Your wall or alcove is under 40 inches wide.

products.name: DICTAC 73.23" Tall Storage Bookcase + 3 Slide-Out Drawers
products.verdict: Three smooth-glide drawers on a 73-inch frame that only needs 24 inches of wall.
products.description:
The DICTAC stretches to 73.23 inches while staying only 23.62 inches wide and 14.2 inches deep. It stacks three slide-out drawers under three open tiers and a top storage zone, and the engineered wood is described as waterproof and scratch resistant.

It lands one place behind the FINETONES because the total open shelf space is smaller, but it wins on footprint: you get closed storage in a column rather than a slab. That moisture-resistant surface is also why owners place it in kitchens and bathrooms, not just bedrooms. An anti-tip kit is in the box, which matters at this height.

Best for narrow walls, hallways and pantry duty. Skip it if you mostly own tall hardcovers, since the tiers are limited.
products.idealFor: Narrow walls, pantries and bathrooms that need closed storage.
products.skipIf: You want lots of open shelving for large books.

products.name: Furologee 5-Tier Bookshelf + 1 Removable Fabric Drawer
products.verdict: The cheapest way in, with a lift-out drawer and a 15-inch footprint.
products.description:
Furologee's standard model pairs a metal frame and P2 MDF shelves with five open tiers and a single removable fabric drawer. It is 15.4 inches wide by 10.6 deep and 55.5 tall, with four adjustable feet and a rated 30 lb per shelf, 150 lb overall.

It ranks third because it offers the least drawer storage here: one soft bin, against three or four hard drawers above. In exchange it is the lowest cost, fits in corners the bigger units cannot, and a lift-out bin has no rails to pinch small fingers.

A smart buy for dorms, kids' rooms and corners, as long as you are fine with one bin and a modest load rating.
pros: Lift-out bin is easy to clean
products.idealFor: Dorms, kids' rooms and tight corners on a budget.

products.name: EXPERLAM 8-Cube Solid Pine Bookshelf + 4 Fabric Storage Bins
products.verdict: Real pine instead of MDF, with four collapsible bins and a flexible cube layout.
products.description:
The EXPERLAM is an eight-cube unit in solid pine, measuring 47 inches long, 11.8 deep and 24 tall. Four collapsible fabric bins with handles, 11 inches on each side, slot into the openings, and two back panels can be removed for a more open look.

It is the only solid wood pick, so it feels sturdier than the MDF units, and it can stand tall, lie flat or act as a room divider. The compromise is that its storage is bins, not rail drawers, and the low 24-inch height means less vertical capacity than the towers above.

Good for kids' rooms and studio apartments where an odor-free finish and flexibility matter more than drawer count.
products.idealFor: Kids' rooms and studios needing a flexible, solid-wood cube unit.
products.skipIf: You want rail-mounted drawers or a tall tower.

products.name: SUNMORY 6-Tier Tree Bookshelf + 2 Storage Cabinets
products.verdict: A tree-shaped shelf with two joinable cabinets and a two-year warranty.
products.description:
The SUNMORY uses a tree-shaped, six-tier layout that branches upward over two open storage cabinets. They can be joined into one wider base, the MDF carries a vintage faux-wood finish, and the shelf is 47.4 inches tall, 14.6 wide and 7.9 deep.

It ranks fifth because the 7.9-inch depth is shallow for anything bigger than paperbacks, and the cabinets are open rather than closed drawers. Its edge is the two-year warranty with lifetime support, which is rare at this tier, and an anti-tip kit is included.

Best for a small bedroom or entryway where a decorative shelf and a bit of backing support matter more than storage volume.
products.idealFor: Small bedrooms and entryways wanting a decorative shelf.
products.skipIf: You need to store large books or closed drawers.

products.name: Furologee 5-Tier Ladder Shelf + 1 Removable Fabric Drawer
products.verdict: Ladder shape widens at the base for a 215 lb total rating.
products.description:
This ladder version of the Furologee widens toward the bottom, measures 16.53 by 11.42 by 55.51 inches and carries a 215 lb total rating. It shares the removable fabric drawer, adds backboards behind each shelf and sits on four adjustable feet with a black metal frame.

Against the standard Furologee above it, you gain about 65 lb of capacity and a back stop that keeps small items from sliding off. You also give up a little floor space and a slightly different look. It stays behind the bigger units because it still offers just one soft drawer.

Pick it if you like the ladder silhouette and want a sturdier version of the entry-level model.
products.idealFor: Buyers who like the ladder look and want more load rating.
products.skipIf: You want more than one drawer.

products.name: Evermagin 6-Tier Tree Bookshelf + Light + 1 Storage Drawer
products.verdict: The only one here with a built-in lamp, but it is a light-duty shelf.
products.description:
The Evermagin builds an adjustable lamp with three color temperatures into a six-tier tree shelf that is 15 inches wide, 7.9 deep and 57.87 tall. A single drawer sits at the base, and the shelves hold an estimated 30 to 50 paperbacks.

The lamp is the reason to look at it, and also why it ranks last: the 7.9-inch depth and one drawer make it the lightest storage option on this list. Against the SUNMORY it adds a lamp and a drawer but offers no extended warranty. An anti-tip kit is included.

Best for a reading nook where a shelf and a lamp in one footprint save a separate light. Not for heavy loads.
products.idealFor: Reading nooks that need a shelf and light in one.
products.skipIf: You store hardcovers or heavy items.

methodology.title: Drawer type and count
methodology.description: We separated rail-mounted drawers from fabric bins and open cabinets, because they solve different clutter problems and fail in different ways.

methodology.title: Footprint versus storage
methodology.description: Width and depth were weighed against total storage zones so a bigger unit had to earn its wall space.

methodology.title: Frame material
methodology.description: Solid pine, thickened engineered wood and thin MDF were ranked by how rigid each should stay across years of load.

methodology.title: Load rating
methodology.description: Stated per-shelf and total capacities were compared against what a typical book collection weighs.

methodology.title: Safety features
methodology.description: Anti-tip hardware and drawer designs were checked, since tall units and small children are a common pairing.

whatMatters.detail: Rail drawers slide on tracks and close out of sight, which hides clutter well but can fail at the track. Fabric bins lift out and collapse, so there is nothing to jam, but they sag and show their contents. Check the listing photos for the drawer front and note whether it says slide-out or removable.

A shelf under about 8 inches deep only suits paperbacks, while hardcovers and binders need 11 inches or more. The depth is often buried in the spec list. Measure your largest book, then compare it with the listed depth before you assume it will fit.

A total rating can hide a weak individual shelf. A full shelf of hardcovers can top 30 lb, so look for the per-shelf figure and not only the whole-unit number. If only a total is listed, divide it by the shelf count to get a rough ceiling.

Solid pine feels sturdiest, thick engineered wood is the middle ground, and thin MDF bows first. The listing usually says P2 MDF, engineered wood or solid wood. Choose the heavier material if the shelf will hold books.

Tall narrow furniture can fall forward when drawers are pulled open. A wall anchor kit prevents that. Look for an anti-tip kit in the box contents, and plan to screw it into a stud, which matters most with children in the home.

faq.q: Are drawers or open shelves better on a bookshelf?
faq.a: Open shelves display and hold books best, while drawers hide small items. If you own both, a unit like the FINETONES that combines four drawers and eight shelves is the better compromise.

faq.q: Can a bookshelf with drawers go in a bathroom or kitchen?
faq.a: Only if the finish is moisture resistant. The DICTAC lists a waterproof, scratch-resistant surface, which is why it suits pantry and bathroom use better than standard MDF.

faq.q: Do I need to anchor a tall bookshelf to the wall?
faq.a: Yes, for anything above about 50 inches. Opening drawers shifts weight forward. Use the included anti-tip kit and fasten it into a stud, especially for the 73-inch DICTAC.

faq.q: Is solid pine worth it over MDF?
faq.a: For heavy books and years of use, yes. Solid pine like the EXPERLAM resists sagging better. For light decor and a few paperbacks, MDF is fine and costs less.

faq.q: How do I stop shelves from sagging under books?
faq.a: Keep heavy volumes on the lowest shelves, stay under the per-shelf rating and avoid spans over about 30 inches without support. Thicker panels, as on the FINETONES, sag less.

faq.q: Can fabric drawers hold heavy items?
faq.a: They suit clothes, toys and lightweight clutter. Anything dense, like tools or stacks of paper, can pull a fabric bin out of shape, so use rail drawers for those.

finalTake: For most rooms the FINETONES Double Wide is the right call, with four drawers and eight shelves in one rigid frame. If your wall is narrow, the DICTAC gives you three drawers on a 24-inch column. On a tight budget, the Furologee 5-Tier is the sensible entry point. Anyone with small children should lean toward the EXPERLAM and its lift-out bins.
